name: Optimal State
author: Luke Garrison

sections.description:
Optimal State, also known as WP Optimal State outside the official repository, is a comprehensive performance and optimization suite designed to keep your WordPress site at peak efficiency. With intelligent database management (backup, restore, safety rollback), automated cleanup routines, and advanced performance features, this plugin will transform your WordPress installation into a lean, fast, and secure powerhouse. Optimal State is a versatile and powerful set of tools suitable for users of all skill levels.

It is essentially four plugins in one:
* Database Cleanup and Optimization
* Database Backup and Restore
* Database Search & Replace
* Caching and Performance Tuning

It can easily replace the following plugins:
UpdraftPlus, WP Rocket, WP Super Cache, WP-Optimize, Better Search Replace, Heartbeat Control, Perfmatters, WP Revisions Control, Clearfy, Advanced Database Cleaner, Autoptimize.

IMPORTANT NOTICE: Optimal State is a powerful optimization suite capable of significant structural changes. Due to its advanced functionalities, this plugin serves as a preview/demo version, allowing administrators to evaluate the interface and features in a risk-free environment before deploying to a live production site. When you’re ready to optimize your actual site, you can upgrade to the Free or Pro version, which provides fully functional capabilities.

Live Interactive Preview | Get Pro Version

Key Features

  • Database Health Monitoring: Real-time scoring system to assess your database’s efficiency and cleanliness
  • One-Click Optimization: Comprehensive optimization with a single click
  • Smart Backup System: Automated database backups with integrity verification
  • Advanced Cleanup Tools: Remove post revisions, spam comments, transients, orphaned data, and more
  • Targeted Optimizations: Specialized tools for WooCommerce, Action Scheduler, oEmbed cache, and unused terms
  • Performance Features:
    • Server-side page caching with smart purge
    • Browser caching via .htaccess rules
    • Database query caching (Redis/Memcached compatible)
    • Lazy loading for images and iframes
    • Heartbeat API control to reduce server load
  • Security Enhancements:
    • Disable XML-RPC, emojis, pingbacks, and unnecessary headers
    • Remove WordPress version, RSD links, and WLW manifest
  • Automation Scheduler: Set-and-forget maintenance with customizable schedules
  • Database Search & Replace: Safe search and replace with serialized data handling
  • User Access Control: Restrict plugin access to specific administrators
  • Settings Export/Import: Backup and migrate your configuration
  • PageSpeed Integration: Analyze Core Web Vitals metrics

Professional Features

  • Intelligent Caching System: Smart cookie detection for GDPR compliance
  • Database Structure Analysis: Detailed insights into your database architecture
  • Performance Metrics Dashboard: Monitor key performance indicators
  • Automated Maintenance: Scheduled cleanup and optimization tasks
  • Comprehensive Logging: Detailed activity logs for all operations
  • Safe Operation Mode: Dry run previews for potentially dangerous operations

  • Google PageSpeed Insights API – Performance measurement tool that analyzes web page content and generates suggestions to make that page faster.
    The plugin’s PageSpeed integration uses this API to fetch and display Core Web Vitals metrics and optimization opportunities.
    When you use the PageSpeed feature, your site URL is sent to Google’s servers for analysis.
    Use of this API is subject to Google’s Terms of Service and Privacy Policy.

    • API Documentation: https://developers.google.com/speed/docs/insights/v5/get-started

Note: The PageSpeed Insights feature is optional and only activates when you manually request a performance analysis. No data is sent to external services without your explicit action.

sections.installation:
Using The WordPress Dashboard

This is the simplest method of installing a plugin.

  1. Log in to your WordPress dashboard
  2. Navigate to “Plugins > Add New”
  3. Find the search form in the top-right and type “optistate”
  4. Find Optimal State plugin card and click “Install Now”
  5. Click “Activate” to activate the plugin
  6. Look for “Optimal State” in your admin menu

Uploading in WordPress Dashboard

  1. Download the “optistate.zip” file from WordPress.org
  2. Log in to your WordPress dashboard
  3. Navigate to “Plugins > Add New”
  4. Click the “Upload Plugin” button at the top of the screen
  5. Choose the “optistate.zip” file from your device
  6. Click “Install Now”
  7. Activate the plugin
  8. Look for “Optimal State” in your admin menu
sections.faq:
What is the difference between the Preview, Free, and Pro versions?

The Preview version (this repository version) allows you to explore the full interface and features, but all operations are simulated – no actual changes are made to your database. The Free version provides full backup, restore, cleanup, and basic caching functionality with limited automation. The Pro version (WP Optimal State Pro) includes advanced features like Search & Replace execution, table repair, autoload optimization, automated scheduling, email notifications, and priority support. See the complete feature comparison in the User Manual tab inside the plugin.

Is it safe to use on my live production site?

Yes, when used properly. Optimal State includes multiple safety features including automatic backups before critical operations, dry-run capabilities for Search & Replace, and detailed warnings before destructive actions. However, we strongly recommend creating a manual backup before running any optimization for the first time, and testing on a staging site first if available.

Will this plugin slow down my website?

No. Optimal State is designed to improve performance, not hinder it. The plugin only runs when you access its admin interface or during scheduled maintenance (which runs during low-traffic periods). The performance features like caching and lazy loading actively speed up your site for visitors.

Can I use this with other caching plugins?

Optimal State includes comprehensive caching features that can replace most caching plugins (WP Rocket, W3 Total Cache, WP Super Cache, LiteSpeed). If you’re already using another caching plugin, you can disable Optimal State’s caching features to avoid conflicts, or disable your existing caching plugin since Optimal State provides equivalent functionality.

How is this different from WP-Optimize or similar plugins?

Optimal State goes beyond basic database cleanup. It includes enterprise-grade features like GZIP-compressed backups with integrity verification, serialization-aware Search & Replace, table defragmentation, corruption repair, autoload optimization, PageSpeed Insights integration, and multi-layer caching (server-side, browser, and database query caching). It’s essentially four plugins in one: database cleaner, backup system, search & replace tool, and performance optimizer.

What happens if I accidentally delete important data?

If you’re using the Free or Pro version, you can immediately restore from your most recent backup. This is why Optimal State emphasizes creating backups before all operations. The Preview version simulates operations without making actual changes, so there’s no risk of data loss.

How often should I run database optimization?

For most sites, weekly optimization is sufficient and can be automated through the Automation tab. High-traffic e-commerce sites may benefit from daily optimization. The plugin’s Health Score indicator (found in the Optimize tab) will help you determine when optimization is needed – scores below 70 indicate it’s time to run cleanup operations.

Does this work with WooCommerce?

Yes! Optimal State includes specialized optimizations for WooCommerce, including cleanup of expired sessions, Action Scheduler logs, transients, and order-related bloat. WooCommerce sites typically accumulate database bloat faster than regular sites, making Optimal State particularly valuable for online stores.

Will optimization delete my posts, pages, or products?

No. Optimal State only removes unnecessary data like post revisions (old versions), spam comments, expired cache, orphaned metadata, and similar clutter. Your published content remains untouched. The only exception is the “Trashed Posts” cleanup, which permanently deletes items already in your WordPress trash – and this requires explicit confirmation.

What are “transients” and why should I clean them?

Transients are WordPress’s way of temporarily caching data. They’re supposed to expire automatically, but WordPress often leaves expired transients in your database indefinitely. Cleaning transients is 100% safe – if WordPress needs that data again, it will regenerate it automatically. This is one of the safest and most impactful cleanups you can perform.

Can I undo an optimization?

Database cleanup operations cannot be undone except by restoring from a backup. This is why the plugin creates automatic backups before operations and strongly encourages manual backups. Performance features (caching, heartbeat control, etc.) are simple toggles and can be turned on/off anytime without risk.

Why don’t I see speed improvements when logged in?

When you’re logged into WordPress as an administrator, Optimal State (and most caching plugins) intentionally bypass the cache. This ensures you can edit your site safely and see changes immediately. To test actual performance improvements, open your site in an Incognito/Private browser window where you’re not logged in – this shows the cached experience your visitors receive.

Does this work with Multisite?

NO. The current version is designed for single-site WordPress installations. Multisite support is planned for a future release. However, you can install Optimal State on individual sites within a multisite network (not network-activated).

What are “orphaned” items and is it safe to remove them?

Orphaned data refers to database entries that reference content that no longer exists – for example, metadata for deleted posts, or category assignments for deleted content. This data serves no purpose and safely removing it improves database efficiency. Optimal State carefully identifies truly orphaned data to ensure no active content is affected.

How do I restore a backup?

In the Backups tab, locate the backup you want to restore and click the Restore button (undo icon). Optimal State will automatically create a safety backup of your current database first, then restore the selected backup. Your site may be briefly in maintenance mode during restoration. Important: Only use this feature in the Free or Pro versions, as the Preview version simulates this action.

What is “table overhead” and why does it matter?

Table overhead is fragmented space within your database tables – essentially wasted space from deleted or modified data. High overhead (>10MB) acts like a fragmented hard drive, slowing down database queries. The “Optimize Tables” feature in the Advanced tab defragments and compacts your tables, reclaiming this space and improving query performance by 15-30%.

Can I schedule automatic backups and cleanups?

Yes, in the Free and Pro versions. The Automation tab allows you to schedule weekly, daily, or monthly maintenance that automatically creates backups and performs optimization. You can also enable email notifications to receive reports after each automated run. The Preview version displays the interface but doesn’t execute scheduled tasks.

What’s the difference between “Expired Transients” and “All Transients”?

“Expired Transients” removes only cache entries that have passed their expiration date – this is 100% safe. “All Transients” removes both expired AND active transients. While still generally safe (WordPress will regenerate needed data), removing all transients may cause a temporary performance dip as the cache rebuilds. Most users should stick with cleaning expired transients only.

Does this plugin collect any data or phone home?

No. Optimal State operates entirely on your server. The only external connection is to Google’s PageSpeed Insights API, and only when you manually click “Run Audit” in the Statistics tab. No usage data, statistics, or personal information is collected or transmitted.

How do I get support?

For the Preview version, consult the comprehensive User Manual tab within the plugin interface. For Free and Pro versions, premium email support is included. Response times are typically within 24-48 hours. When contacting support, include your WordPress version, PHP version, hosting provider, and any error messages from the Activity Log. Support Page

My health score is low – what should I do?

A low health score (below 70) indicates your database needs attention. Start by clicking “Refresh Analysis” to ensure the score is current. Then, create a backup and run “One-Click Optimization” from the Optimize tab. This will clean revisions, spam, transients, and overhead. If the score remains low, review the Statistics tab to identify specific problem areas and use targeted cleanup operations.

What is Search & Replace and when would I use it?

Search & Replace is a powerful tool for finding and replacing text throughout your entire database. Common uses include: changing your domain name (http://oldsite.com to https://newsite.com), updating file paths after server migration, or making bulk content changes. Warning: This tool is extremely powerful and mistakes cannot be undone. Always perform a dry run first, review results carefully, and ensure you have a recent backup.

Can I use Optimal State on shared hosting?

Yes! Optimal State is designed to work on all hosting environments including shared hosting. The plugin respects server limits for memory, execution time, and disk space. If you’re on very restrictive shared hosting, you may need to increase PHP memory_limit and max_execution_time in your hosting control panel or .htaccess file for optimal performance.
